Details: setup_of_a_sealed_sandbox_is_refused_before_it_takes_the_host at tensorlake_add_tests.rs:2033-2068 records note_sealed, compares manager.state before/after start_add (2047-2048,2058-2061), and checks only that backend events are empty (2063-2067). manager.state at manager.rs:2237-2238 delegates to status, whose 2214-2224 replaces the actor's state with sealed_state for any recorded seal. sealed_state at 2669-2679 returns Deleting solely from the independent sealed map. Meanwhile hold_connection at 1655-1695 does not refuse a sealed host: it changes underlying actor state, removes its client, advances incarnation and sets status.hold at 1663-1672 without changing that map. Thus moving the refusal in tensorlake_add.rs:894-900 to after the hold at 905-913 would leave both compared public states equal, retain the same being-deleted error and execute no provisioning backend action; this test would not distinguish the forbidden hold from the intended ordering.
